issues.failure_explanation: The proof treats the invisible component $u_F$ as if its $L^2$ norm were equivalent to the endpoint values $u_F(t_{T+1})$. For large $|T|\lambda$, the invisible quadratic $q_T$ has $q_T(t_T)=1$ but $q_T(t_{T+1})\sim 2/(|T|\lambda)$, so the endpoint values do not control the $L^2$ norm. Taking $u=q_T e_i$ on a large time step gives an ansatz function orthogonal to $Y_T$, with $\int (\partial_t+\lambda)u\,v=0$ for all $v\in Y_T$, while $\|u\|_{X_\lambda}\sim\sqrt{\lambda|T|}$ and the initial term is $O(1)$. Hence the claimed uniform inf-sup constant cannot hold.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must control the large-$|T|\lambda$ invisible boundary-layer mode, either by changing the test space/ansatz space, adding a stronger norm, or restricting to a regime where $|T|\lambda$ is uniformly bounded.
issues.overall_effect: The discrete inf-sup stability theorem and all downstream optimality, reliability, Céa, and model-order-reduction convergence results become unsupported.
issues.title: False large-step inf-sup lemma: invisible mode is not controlled
issues.why_classification: The false lemma is the core of the inf-sup proof; without it the main optimality theorem and its applications do not survive.

issues.failure_explanation: The estimator uses $\partial_t f$, but the model problem only assumes $f\in L^2(0,\tend;V^\star)$. Lemma \ref{lem:reliability} proves the needed reliability under the stronger hypothesis $f\in\SS^2(\TT;V^\star)$, but Theorem \ref{thm:optimal_timestepping} does not include this or any other differentiability assumption on $f$. Thus the estimator may be undefined and the reliability step does not apply to the stated theorem.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a sufficient regularity assumption on $f$, such as $f\in H^1(0,\tend;V^\star)$ or $f\in\SS^2(\TT;V^\star)$ for all admissible meshes, and restate the main theorem under that assumption.
issues.overall_effect: The main optimality theorem is not proved for the general $L^2$ right-hand side stated in the model problem; the adaptive algorithm may not be computable from the stated data.
issues.title: Estimator and main theorem need regularity of f
issues.why_classification: The repair is a standard added regularity hypothesis, but it narrows the advertised $L^2$ data scope.

issues.failure_explanation: The space $X_R^{(\mathrm{rb})}$ consists of functions taking values in the reduced space $V_R^{(\mathrm{rb})}$. The difference $u_h-\mathsf P_R^{(\mathrm{rb})}u_h$ and the total error $u_h-u_{R,\TT_\ell}^{(\mathrm{rb})}$ are not in general elements of $V_R^{(\mathrm{rb})}$, so their $X_R^{(\mathrm{rb})}$-norms are undefined. The proof also uses reduced-space norms on $u_h-\mathsf P_Ru_h$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the reduced-space norm on the full error/projection difference by the corresponding norm on $X_h$ (or $X$), while keeping reduced norms only for quantities that actually lie in the reduced space.
issues.overall_effect: The main MOR convergence statements are ill-defined as written; the intended comparison must be made in a norm defined on the full space or after projecting the error.
issues.title: Ill-defined reduced-space norms in MOR error bounds
issues.why_classification: The defect is a systematic norm-space mismatch affecting several MOR theorems, but it has a clear local notational repair.

issues.failure_explanation: The Hardy-space norm equals the weighted $L^2_\alpha$ norm on $\mathbb R_+$. For the finite interval $[0,\tend]$, the weight $e^{-\alpha t}$ gives a factor $e^{2\alpha\tend}$ when converting squared norms, not $e^{\alpha\tend}$. Thus the displayed inequality undercounts the exponential factor by $e^{\alpha\tend}$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace $e^{\alpha\tend}$ by $e^{2\alpha\tend}$ in the Paley-Wiener conversion and in subsequent constants depending on it.
issues.overall_effect: The MOR error bounds contain an incorrect constant factor; the exponential rate in $R$ or $M$ is unaffected, but the displayed bounds are not literally correct.
issues.title: Incorrect Paley-Wiener exponential factor
issues.why_classification: The error is a routine exponential constant factor and does not change any convergence rate or structural claim.
